about.title: Placerville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Placerville's small-town streets carry a surprising amount of traffic pressure, especially where Route 50 and US-50 funnel commuters and travelers through town alongside Placerville Drive and Broadway Drive. El Dorado County's own crash counts show dozens of injury collisions each year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. a recurring high point. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: insurers move fast, evidence disappears, and California's statute of limitations starts running immediately. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured people in Placerville with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain your options, and handle communication with insurance companies on your behalf. There's no cost to get connected, and attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover something. You don't have to figure this out alone or guess at deadlines while trying to heal.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a county road crew or a public agency vehicle — is involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can collect. Insurers know this and often try to shift blame onto you early, sometimes during a recorded statement you're not required to give.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but that doesn't mean insurers offer them freely. An attorney working on contingency has an incentive to push for a fair evaluation of your losses, and you pay nothing unless there's a recovery.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift blame or minimize your claim later. An attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Route 50 or US-50 near Placerville?
items.answer: Corridors like Route 50 and US-50 see a meaningful share of Placerville's injury collisions, and depending on how the crash occurred, evidence like traffic camera footage, skid marks, or CHP reports can matter. Acting quickly to preserve that evidence can make a real difference in a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Placerville car accident?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit, but if a government entity is involved — such as a county-maintained road — that window can shrink to as little as six months. It's worth having an attorney confirm your specific deadline early rather than assuming you have the full two years.
